Summary lines:
- Total clusters sampled: 6
- Top recurring idle percentile windows: 02:00-06:00 (EU/AP batch-heavy)
- Mean hourly idle across pools: 32.6%
- Pools with chronic microbursts (>5/hr median): realtime-high, realtime-mid

Quick observations (notes-to-self style):
- realtime-high pools show best avg occupancy but still noisy microbursts (short spikes that increase scheduling churn). Likely due to many small short-lived requests from "search-embed" and "conversational" teams.
- Batch pools (batch-low / batch-medium) are high-idle by design but appear to cluster around 12:00-16:00 and 00:00-03:00. Confirm cron schedules and consider staggering.
- Private-dedicated pool in ap-south-2 is at ~97% avg occupancy for the hour sample. This is a red flag for SLA headroom — flag to SRE + account owner.
- RTL-cache pool shows quick recovery after restarts but creates warm-up idle slices that distort short-term aggregation (we should add 6h rolling exclude after restarts).

Action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Evan: add per-job duration histogram for realtime-high for last 7 days (JIRA:INFRA-4321).
- [ ] Marta: cross-check cron windows for batch-medium and recommend stagger plan; share plan by 2026-04-06.
- [ ] Priya: open urgent alert for enterprise-xyz private pool saturation and propose temporary soft-quota vs burst fallback.
- [ ] Kenji: iterate on the dashboard query to exclude nodes under maintenance from hourly aggregates.

Investigation notes / leads:
- Live slack thread: #infra-gpu-ops (see pinned message, thread ts 1649824000) for restarts and cache warmups.
- Confluence draft with sampling methodology: confluence://infra/hourly-entropy-methodology (link above).

Proposed quick mitigations (cheap wins):
- Apply short-term 10% non-preemptible buffer to private-dedicated pools when avg occupancy > 92% to avoid SLA breaches.
- Implement jitter on batch cron jobs (random 0-10m) for high-frag pools to reduce simultaneous slot demand.
- Run targeted job packing for small realtime requests: encourage batching client-side or enable request coalescing in the routing layer for repeated small requests.

Context/why this sheet exists (short):
This export is a compact snapshot used by infra + SRE to prioritize short-term remediations (staggering crons, buffer adjustments, and routing tweaks) versus longer-term capacity purchases. It's intentionally noisy (hourly level) to surface microburst patterns that daily/weekly aggregates hide.
